runtime: ISO/IEC 9899:2024 C standard library (WG14 N3220); glibc 2.43 libresolv (Ubuntu 2.43-2ubuntu2.7, pinned image) verified; musl inventoried separately

verified_apis.name: glibc libresolv ns_initparse/ns_parserr
verified_apis.api: ns_initparse(msg, msglen, &handle) + ns_parserr(&handle, section, index, &rr) (glibc libresolv, <arpa/nameser.h>)
verified_apis.documentation_note: The glibc manual does not describe ns_initparse; the API is declared in <arpa/nameser.h> (BIND 8 resolver heritage, implemented in resolv/ns_parse.c) and documented by that header and the BIND resolver documentation.
verified_apis.input_api: int ns_initparse(const unsigned char *msg, int msglen, ns_msg *handle); int ns_parserr(ns_msg *handle, ns_sect section, int rrnum, ns_rr *rr)
verified_apis.scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
verified_apis.note: Names come from ns_rr_name and ns_name_uncompress, addresses from inet_ntop, the MX preference from ns_get16; ns_msg_getflag exposes ns_f_z, ns_f_ad and ns_f_cd separately, so z carries all three. glibc is the system runtime and is not source-instrumented here: no parser coverage or AFL++ feedback is claimed, and the path stays outside the third-party ranking.

official_documentation_checked.finding: ISO C defines no DNS message type or parser.

glibc ships the BIND 8 ns_initparse/ns_parserr message parser in libresolv and declares it in <arpa/nameser.h>. The glibc manual does not document it; documentation is the header and BIND 8 resolver heritage. Verified on both controls with adapters/c/dns/libresolv.c (see verified_apis).
musl provides the same interface in libc. Not run.

limit: ISO C has no DNS parser. The glibc libresolv path is a C library runtime API verified on the two valid controls only, without source instrumentation or AFL++ feedback; musl's ns_initparse was not run. Both stay outside the third-party ranking.
